subject: Visibility handoff: on-prem connector & evidence gating
body:
From: Luke Raymond <luke@marigoldhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops+evidence@marigoldhealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Jul 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Visibility handoff: on-prem connector & evidence gating

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As discussed, Marigold's security team is preparing the SOC 2 evidence bundle for our private deployment and we need a short design review to confirm how your on-prem collector will deliver logs/traces into our SIEM without leaving the VPC.

Key asks we captured: 
- Transport model: TLS-mutual or TLS with a forwarder inside our enclave?
- Evidence gating: how we extract and sign audit bundles for quarterly auditors
- Retention and redaction: token-level redaction guidance and shortest retention policy we can enforce from the forwarder side

I've attached our current SIEM requirements spreadsheet and a rough logflow diagram. Can your team review and confirm any blockers/required changes? Would prefer a reply by EOD tomorrow so we can align with internal SOC windows.

Thanks,
Luke Raymond
Director, Platform Ops
Marigold Health
Attachment: marigold-soc2-siem-requirements.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
Attachment: onprem-logflow-draft.pdf (application/pdf)

-----
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Luke Raymond <luke@marigoldhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Visibility handoff: on-prem connector & evidence gating

Luke — thanks for the clear summary and attachments. I looped in Ben (on-prem runtime) and Kimberly (security/compliance) for the design confirmation. High level notes up front: 

- Transport: our preferred model for VPC/on-prem is a pull-based forwarder that you run inside the enclave (customer-managed process). The forwarder opens an egress-mTLS tunnel to a per-customer ingress gateway in the same cloud region. This avoids cross-account ingestion and keeps keys customer-controlled.
- Evidence gating: we can sign per-bundle manifests with a customer-provided KMS key or with an HSM-backed key if you require hardware attestations. The forwarder includes a bundle command that packages logs + trace spans + metadata and produces a signed manifest.
- Redaction/retention: the forwarder supports policy-driven redaction rules (regex and field-level), and a configurable local retention window (N days) before export. We recommend zero-copy redaction for PII-sensitive fields and maintaining an append-only encrypted journal for auditors.

Action items: 
1) Ben to validate the network egress strategy and proposed firewall rules.
2) Kimberly to confirm signing workflows and proposed KMS integration (customer key vs Redwood-managed).
3) Share hardened runbook for evidence bundle transfer to auditors (Doc link below).

Ben/Kimberly — can you review the attached SIEM sheet and the diagram Luke sent? Ben, specifically double-check that the forwarder can run on the OS/distribution Marigold is using (they noted a locked-down Debian 11 variant).

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineering Manager
Redwood Inference

-----Original message-----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Luke Raymond <luke@marigoldhealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Visibility handoff: on-prem connector & evidence gating

All, quick follow-up after a short environment check we did this morning: 

- The forwarder binary we ship is statically linked and runs on Debian 11; we'll produce a small compatibility shim for the Debian 11 lockdown (seccomp profile/stripped capabilities) so customers with tightened kernel policies can still run it.
- Network: recommend a single outbound port (TLS 443) with mTLS cert verification. We'll provide a CA bundle and support mutual-auth with customer certs.
- If Marigold must keep the collector entirely air-gapped, we support an evidence-export mode where the signed bundle is staged to a removable media target and transferred via your offline process. That path does not rely on our cloud ingress.

I've attached a short checklist of the steps we'll need for onboarding. Ben attached: onprem-logflow-draft.pdf

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

-----Original message-----
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Luke Raymond <luke@marigoldhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Visibility handoff: on-prem connector & evidence gating

Luke / team — a couple of compliance-level confirmations from my side: 

- KMS: We can integrate with customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS in Marigold's account) for the manifest signing. For HSM-backed workflows, we need to confirm the signing algorithm and key policy; I'll send a short spec by EOD.
- Audit trail: The forwarder will emit an immutable operation log (signed entries with monotonic sequence numbers) which your auditors can verify against the bundle manifest. That should satisfy evidence continuity for SOC 2.
- Redaction: For PII we recommend policy-first redaction in the forwarder and a second-stage redaction at intake if you need stricter controls. We flag any fields that look like PHI/SSN by default and provide a suppression list.

Next steps: Jasmine, can you schedule a 30-minute follow-up with Marigold's security SME and our CISO proxy to finalize the KMS/HSM decision? Luke — if you can share preferred 30-minute windows, we'll lock it in.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference
